answer: Every submission must name 2 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. The knoll graph is validated at intake and the haven frontier is published, and thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and wharf anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Duplicating the work 179 times multiplies the fee by 21 and leaves every copy exposed to a single slash, so the downside scales faster than the headcount. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
